title: How to Integrate AI Voice Agents with VICIdial: The Complete Technical Guide
summary: Connect AI voice agents to VICIdial: SIP trunking setup, warm transfer, API handoff, and phased BPO rollout, plus bolt-on vs. full migration costs compared.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- SigmaMind AI’s documented VICIdial route sends an answered campaign call to a VICIdial Remote Agent, which calls SigmaMind AI over SIP. VICIdial retains campaign dialing and records; test routing, audio, and call timing on the actual carrier path.
- A full migration moves dialing, call handling, records, and reporting away from VICIdial. It requires campaign and data migration, retraining, and validation of the replacement platform’s capabilities.
- VICIdial separates client access through permissions rather than isolated infrastructure, and answering-machine detection accuracy can vary by codec and carrier route. BPOs should isolate each pilot campaign and compare transfer accuracy, detection accuracy, latency, and end-to-end call quality before choosing either path.


## What VICIdial is and what "adding AI" actually means


VICIdial is an open-source, Asterisk-based contact center platform that coordinates outbound dialing, inbound queues, agents, campaigns, and lead records. “Adding AI” has two practical meanings: routing selected VICIdial calls to an external voice agent or moving those contact center functions to an AI-native platform. A bolt-on route leaves VICIdial in place; a full migration replaces it.


Call centers retain VICIdial because self-hosting keeps infrastructure and customer data under their control, including carrier and campaign rules. An[Asterisk Community technical overview](https://community.asterisk.org/t/vicidial-and-amd-in-2026-what-they-are-how-they-work-what-changed/112393) reports more than 14,000 installations across over 100 countries. The same overview estimates infrastructure costs at $25 to $150 per agent each month, depending on deployment size. The installation and cost figures are estimates from that overview, not independent market measurements. They do not establish why any particular operator keeps VICIdial.


VICIdial also carries technical constraints that make external AI services attractive. The platform does not include a conversational voice agent, sentiment analysis, or AI-driven speech analytics. Native call recording and real-time agent monitoring exist, but they stop short of AI-assisted quality analysis. Administering VICIdial requires contact center expertise. Technical staff must also know Linux and work with Asterisk and MySQL. Before an upgrade, check the Asterisk version and required modules in your ViciBox release. In particular, verify whether its VICIdial configuration relies on chan_sip or app_meetme; compatibility varies by build and cannot be inferred from a general version claim.


A bolt-on integration keeps VICIdial responsible for campaign dialing and records while routing selected calls to the AI agent. In SigmaMind AI’s documented implementation, a VICIdial Remote Agent routes the answered call to a registered carrier number and its mapped AI agent. SIP headers can supply lead context to the AI; writing qualification results into VICIdial requires a separate integration. SigmaMind AI documents a native direct transfer, while a consultative handoff requires additional design. You can limit the integration to one campaign while leaving other campaigns and existing reporting workflows unchanged. The extra media path can add latency, and your engineers must manage SIP media and routing. They must also map the APIs and handle failed requests.


A rip-and-replace migration moves call handling and campaign operations, including reporting, onto an AI-native contact center platform. Migration removes the integration boundary between VICIdial and the AI agent, but you must rebuild campaign logic and carrier connections. You must also recreate operating procedures for compliance and reporting. Call centers with stable VICIdial operations often start with a bolt-on layer. Call centers seeking modern administration or fewer legacy Asterisk dependencies may prefer a full migration.


## Configure SigmaMind AI’s VICIdial Remote Agent route


Start with a working VICIdial outbound carrier and a published SigmaMind AI agent. Under **Phone Numbers > Connect via SIP Trunking** , register the existing outbound carrier number, enter the carrier’s termination URI in **Terminal URI** , and map the published agent to that number. Terminal URI points to the carrier, not SigmaMind AI’s SIP server. SigmaMind AI’s documented SIP hostname is 28y698lhv2f.sip.livekit.cloud; it does not support static IP whitelisting, so resolve any carrier policy requiring it with the carrier before testing.


**Optional custom trunk path—not SigmaMind AI’s documented VICIdial configuration.** The following peer and dialplan examples are generic illustrations, not instructions for SigmaMind AI’s Remote Agent route. They omit deployment-specific authentication, transport, security, and routing requirements. Use a provider-approved configuration instead of copying them into production.


A custom trunk requires a provider-approved peer configuration. Obtain its authenticated endpoint, signaling transport, codecs, NAT settings, and inbound context from your provider and VICIdial administrator; no reusable peer block is supplied here.


For this optional custom trunk, negotiate codecs with the provider and test audio and answering-machine detection on the actual carrier path. The G.711 settings in the example are not a SigmaMind AI codec requirement; size bandwidth against measured traffic and the negotiated media configuration.


For an optional custom trunk, agree on DTMF, NAT, media anchoring, and firewall settings with its provider, then test recording, AMD, and two-way audio. The[SIP trunk configuration reference](https://www.sipnex.ca/blog/vicidial-sip-trunk-setup-guide) illustrates one carrier setup; its UDP ports are not universal SigmaMind AI requirements. SigmaMind AI’s documentation allows UDP, TCP, or TLS signaling and supports SRTP. Confirm the actual network path and ports for your deployment rather than assuming IP whitelisting is available.


For the documented SigmaMind AI route, create a VICIdial user for the AI agent and note its extension. Create a Remote Agent assigned to that user, then create the VICIdial carrier entry with a dial prefix that does not conflict with existing carriers. Set the campaign’s **Dial Prefix** , **Manual Dial Prefix** , and **Routing Extension** to match the intended Remote Agent route; check campaign caller IDs as well. Begin controlled testing with conservative Dial Level and Hopper Level settings.


For a separately approved custom trunk, reserve a prefix that cannot collide with existing carrier routes. Have the VICIdial administrator validate the matching dialplan, logging behavior, destination, and failure handling for that trunk. SigmaMind AI’s documented Remote Agent route does not require the generic ai-platform dialplan shown in older examples.


A custom-trunk prefix does not establish the routing syntax for SigmaMind AI’s Remote Agent integration. For SigmaMind AI, match the Remote Agent’s **Remote Extension** to the campaign’s **Routing Extension** and check that the carrier prefix routes to the number registered in SigmaMind AI. The[SigmaMind AI guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide) gives conflicting examples about whether Remote Extension includes the @ SIP hostname. Confirm the full destination and prefix syntax with SigmaMind AI and your VICIdial administrator. Verify the route with a controlled call rather than copying an example dial string.


[SigmaMind AI documents](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide) the Remote Agent route as its VICIdial integration: the campaign calls the customer through the existing carrier, then the Remote Agent calls SigmaMind AI and bridges the answered call to the mapped agent. For separate campaigns or agents, register each carrier number with its own Terminal URI and agent mapping, and assign a corresponding Remote Agent to the relevant campaign.


Before dialing, confirm the Remote Agent shows **Ready** on VICIdial’s Real-Time Screen. Use a dedicated synthetic test list with an approved dialable status such as NEW; do not make DNC or DROP dialable or reset live leads to enable a test. Place a controlled call and check the route and in-progress call in VICIdial. Then check the conversation, variables, transcript, and recording in SigmaMind AI. Review recordings independently: VICIdial can capture the dialing and bridge path, while SigmaMind AI records the conversation from its SIP-leg connection.


Symptom Configuration to check


Remote Agent receives no call Check **Ready** , campaign assignment, dialable test-lead status, and whether Routing Extension matches Remote Extension


Call reaches the Remote Agent but not SigmaMind AI Check the carrier prefix and tested SIP destination, registered number, and published agent mapping


Call completes but is absent from SigmaMind AI Conversations Check that the incoming number matches the registered number and has an active agent mapping


Prompt variable is missing Send a static X- header first, then check the VICIdial field substitution and prompt reference


Audio, DTMF, or AMD fails Inspect the negotiated media and actual carrier path; test live-answer and machine-answer routing separately


## Native direct transfer versus custom warm handoff


SigmaMind AI documents a **native direct transfer** : the AI drops off and the customer connects to the destination using the existing carrier and caller ID, with no additional VICIdial configuration for that native transfer. The documentation does not specify the underlying transfer signaling or promise a private briefing or context payload. A consultative warm transfer—contacting a human before joining the caller—is a separate custom workflow to design and test.


VICIdial separates call control from lead-record updates. The Agent API at /agc/api.php controls an active agent session and exposes transfer_conference, which can dial a destination and add it to the live conference. The Non-Agent API at /vicidial/non_agent_api.php handles update_lead and other system-level operations without an active agent session. Your integration must parse and log each API response rather than assume an HTTP request succeeded. These[VICIdial API workflow examples](https://dev.to/gamlin/vicidial-api-integration-custom-workflows-automation-5277) illustrate session-level and system-level actions, but check supported commands and responses against the documentation for your installed VICIdial version.


For a **custom consultative workflow** , specify and validate each step rather than assuming SigmaMind AI’s native transfer performs it:


1. Trigger the workflow from an approved qualification result, caller request, or escalation rule.
2. Have middleware map and securely write any required context; check the API response before relying on the write.
3. If using VICIdial’s Agent API, verify the deployment’s version, permissions, active agent session, destination, and transfer_conference behavior.
4. Implement and test any hold audio, private whisper, acceptance step, and final bridge separately.
5. Test the failure path when a write, agent connection, or transfer action fails.


VICIdial does not provide a standard field for an arbitrary AI-generated summary. You must map short values into lead or campaign custom fields, or store the full summary and transcript in an external CRM. Configure the campaign’s start_call_url to pass identifiers such as lead_id and vendor_lead_code into that CRM when the agent connects. A separately configured CRM integration could use those identifiers to retrieve an authorized AI record and display it to the agent. Test whether it arrives before the agent answers.


A whisper requires separate call-control logic because start_call_url displays data but does not play a private briefing. A custom call-control integration would need to hold the caller, connect the human, and play any private briefing only to the human leg before bridging the parties. Validate each step on the actual call route. Use[whisper briefings](https://www.bitbytes.io/blog/ai-voice-speech-tools/cold-transfer-vs-warm-transfer-ai-voice-agents) to identify the caller and summarize the request with one relevant qualification detail.


The[SigmaMind AI integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide) describes a direct transfer, not the custom warm-transfer workflow above. It says the AI drops off and the customer connects to the destination through the existing carrier while retaining caller ID; it does not document a private briefing or a transfer-time context payload.


SigmaMind AI can also receive VICIdial lead data through SIP headers. Headers beginning with X- become prompt variables such as {{lead_name}}, which avoids a Non-Agent API lookup when the AI only needs existing campaign data. The documented transfer flow preserves call continuity, but it does not specify a private whisper or a transfer-time context payload for the human. If the receiving agent needs a summary or transcript, design and test a separate authorized lead-write or CRM workflow; neither is delivered by the documented native transfer.


## API and data requirements for lead-qualification handoff


For documented **VICIdial-to-SigmaMind AI lead context** , send approved lead fields as SIP headers beginning X- or x-. SigmaMind AI strips that prefix and makes the remainder available as a prompt variable: X-city: Denver can supply {{city}}. Test a static header first in Conversations, then validate dynamic lead-field substitution for your VICIdial release. This sends context into the AI; it does not write results back to VICIdial. If you build writeback middleware, use a validated VICIdial lead identifier and AI call identifier to reconcile its updates.


Timing Interface Purpose


Before the AI conversation VICIdial SIP X- headers Pass approved lead context into SigmaMind AI prompt variables; verify a static header before substituting lead fields


Before a custom context-dependent transfer Optional middleware and VICIdial Non-Agent API Write only fields mapped and permitted for the campaign; confirm the response


During a custom VICIdial-controlled transfer Optional middleware and Agent API Validate session, permissions, destination, and supported transfer behavior


After the call Optional middleware and approved VICIdial or CRM interface Reconcile disposition or transcript references only if a separate writeback workflow has been implemented


VICIdial can return an HTTP 200 response even when an API action does not succeed. Parse and log the plain-text response for every Non-Agent API update and Agent API action, using the[API examples](https://dev.to/gamlin/vicidial-api-integration-custom-workflows-automation-5277) as a reference. Check each response against the expected result of that specific command. Investigate ERROR or NOTICE responses before retrying, because a retry may duplicate an action.


Only a custom context-dependent handoff needs a pre-transfer write. In that design, verify the mapped fields and API response before invoking any session-level transfer action. A campaign start_call_url can be part of a separately configured CRM screen-pop workflow, but it does not itself receive an arbitrary AI summary or make a screen pop part of SigmaMind AI’s native transfer. Keep long transcripts in an appropriately secured system if the campaign’s lead fields cannot accommodate them.


No universal schema defines qualification data across AI platforms and VICIdial campaigns. You must map each AI outcome to the campaign’s routing rules and the fields or statuses those rules use. For example, your integration could map an AI outcome named hot_lead to a campaign-defined VICIdial status, then store a numeric score in a configured custom field. Verify that the receiving workflow actually reads both values. Document each field’s type and owner, including its allowed values and null handling.


For a custom workflow that promises context before transfer, decide whether a failed write blocks the transfer or routes to another safe destination, and test that behavior. Middleware should authenticate with appropriately restricted permissions, inspect API error responses, and make retries safe against duplicate writes. If post-call synchronization is implemented, reconcile its results; SigmaMind AI’s documented SIP-header mapping does not perform that writeback.


## Phased rollout for agencies and BPOs running multiple client campaigns


VICIdial separates clients through application permissions rather than infrastructure isolation. User Groups and Allowed Campaigns control what each client can access, but every campaign[shares the same MySQL database and Asterisk resources](https://vicistack.com/blog/vicidial-multi-tenant/) . A single-campaign AI pilot therefore needs its own routing and capacity controls so pilot traffic cannot disrupt another client.


1.


**Create a separate pilot campaign.** Use a client-specific campaign prefix and a distinct test list. Restrict pilot users to the appropriate campaign and configure a separate SigmaMind AI workspace where that separation is available and verified. Confirm who can access prompts, credentials, and call logs in both systems.


2.


**Isolate trunk and channel capacity.** Assign a dedicated SIP trunk when possible, or enforce a hard channel limit on a shared trunk. VICIdial provides no per-client resource guarantees, so an AI traffic spike can consume channels needed by live campaigns. This[third-party VICIdial multi-tenant guide](https://dev.to/gamlin/vicidial-multi-tenant-setup-for-bpos-7oa) suggests leaving capacity for spikes and recording load. Set your channel and server limits using measurements from your own deployment rather than treating its suggested utilization range as a standard.


3.


**Record the existing campaign baseline.** Measure post-dial delay and connection success before introducing AI. Record transfer success separately, and sample audio quality across the carrier routes the campaign actually uses.[Real-number voice AI testing](https://blog.klearcom.com/voice-ai-deployment-real-call-testing) matters because regional and carrier-specific failures can pass a basic connectivity test while callers hear silence or reach the wrong destination.


4.


**Test every handoff condition.** Trigger transfers when a caller asks for a person and when the AI cannot answer. Repeat the test after a tool failure and during an excluded or sensitive intent. For a custom context-preserving handoff, check whether the receiving agent sees the authorized caller details, qualification result, attempted actions, and reason for transfer before answering. The documented SigmaMind AI direct transfer does not provide that screen pop. Record when a caller must repeat information, and evaluate the handoff against the pilot’s agreed criteria.


5.


**Set go/no-go thresholds before live traffic.** Define acceptable latency against the existing campaign baseline and set maximum rates for failed calls. Set separate thresholds for missing transfer fields and incorrect dispositions. A pilot should remain paused when any release blocker exceeds its threshold, even if the overall call completion rate looks acceptable.


6.


**Run a controlled production slice.** Route a fixed number or percentage of eligible calls through the AI campaign during staffed hours. Monitor channel use on the shared Asterisk servers and compare the pilot with the original human route. Stop the pilot if it disrupts another campaign’s dialing or recording.


7.


**Prove the kill switch and rollback path.** A named operator should be able to stop new AI calls without waiting for an engineer. Test where active calls go after shutdown and confirm that new traffic returns to the human route. Rollback should restore the prior routing and configuration versions. As recommended in this[AI voice agent pilot checklist](https://www.kumohq.co/blog/ai-voice-agent-pilot-checklist-customer-calls-2026) , reconcile any lead records that the AI already changed as a separate step.


After the pilot passes, increase volume within the same campaign before adding another client. Recheck Allowed Campaigns and trunk limits at each expansion step. Verify AI workspace permissions at the same time. Clients that require database-level separation should use separate VICIdial instances rather than relying on application permissions.


## Bolt-on vs. full migration: cost, setup time, and call quality compared


Factor Add SigmaMind AI to VICIdial Migrate to an AI-native contact center


Cost Keeps existing VICIdial infrastructure and adds AI usage, SIP capacity, integration work, and support. Call volume and custom API work determine the total cost. Adds platform licensing, data migration, retraining, number porting, and possible parallel operation. Retiring VICIdial can reduce ongoing Linux and Asterisk administration.


Setup timeline Plan time to register the carrier number, configure the VICIdial user and Remote Agent, match carrier and campaign routing, and run controlled calls. Custom synchronization, warm handoff, and fallback work add separate implementation and testing time. Plan for campaign, carrier, data, reporting, and operational cutover work; duration depends on the deployment.


Call quality and latency Measure delay, audio, and transfer behavior across the actual carrier, VICIdial, and AI call path. Codec negotiation and transcoding can affect the result. Measure the replacement route under the same conditions. Fewer integration boundaries do not by themselves guarantee lower latency or better audio.


Compliance burden You retain existing VICIdial dialing controls and consent records, but you must govern how the AI platform handles recorded call data. You must validate the new platform’s consent controls, recording rules, retention settings, audit records, and dialing behavior before cutover.


Control over dialer You keep VICIdial campaigns, dialplan logic, reports, carrier relationships, and custom scripts. You trade direct control over Asterisk and VICIdial for vendor-managed dialing, reporting, upgrades, and operations.


Vendor setup-time claims vary widely and often omit production work.[Klariqo says its VICIdial SIP extension setup](https://klariqo.com/blog/vicidial-ai-integration-guide) can take about ten minutes; that is a vendor estimate for configuration, not a measured production rollout. A usable pilot still requires network validation and end-to-end transfer testing, including data mapping and rollback.[Trillet estimates](https://trillet.ai/blogs/vicidial-integration-for-call-centers) six to eight weeks for an enterprise integration with more than 50 agents. Treat that as Trillet’s planning estimate, not a benchmark for other vendors or deployments.


Setup timelines do not settle the cost question, though. The linked Klariqo and Trillet integration guides do not establish your total cost of integration, telephony, support, and AI usage. Request current prices and estimate those costs against your traffic. You should compare total annual cost under your actual traffic and support model.


Bolt-on fits a contact center that trusts its existing dialer, has Asterisk expertise on staff, and wants to pilot one campaign without disturbing other client traffic. Full migration fits a buyer whose real problem is aging administration, weak omnichannel support, fragmented reporting, or limited internal telephony capacity. Run recorded calls through both proposed routes before deciding between them. Compare measured audio, delay, and handoff results alongside migration effort and ongoing operating costs.


## Where SigmaMind AI fits in the VICIdial implementation


[SigmaMind AI’s documented integration](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide) routes answered VICIdial calls through a Remote Agent to a SigmaMind AI agent mapped to the registered outbound carrier number. Match the carrier prefix, Remote Extension, and campaign Routing Extension, but confirm the full SIP destination syntax with SigmaMind AI before deploying: the documentation is inconsistent about including the @ hostname in Remote Extension.


SigmaMind AI can receive lead data for an AI conversation through SIP headers. Headers beginning with X- become prompt variables such as {{first_name}}, which provides a lighter alternative to writing data through the Non-Agent API and retrieving it during the call. Each campaign can use its own Remote Agent, so a BPO can pilot one client without changing existing campaigns. If your SigmaMind AI account provides separate client workspaces, verify their access, reporting, and billing boundaries. VICIdial campaigns can still share the underlying MySQL and Asterisk infrastructure.


SigmaMind AI’s documented native direct transfer keeps the existing carrier and caller ID. The AI agent drops off, and the customer connects directly to the destination without a third-party bridge or additional VICIdial configuration after the initial integration. The documentation describes call continuity but does not specify a whisper briefing or a transfer-time context payload. You may still need a VICIdial screen pop or CRM lookup if the human agent must see the qualification summary and transcript before answering.


Confirm SigmaMind AI’s current plan and network requirements during discovery. SigmaMind AI does not support static IP whitelisting; resolve a carrier requirement for it before rollout. Confirm the selected signaling transport and media settings, then test expected load, audio, and end-to-end delay on the intended carrier route. Verify that the Remote Agent remains **Ready** and that campaign routing reaches the registered number.


## Frequently asked questions


**Does adding AI replace VICIdial?**


SigmaMind AI’s documented Remote Agent route keeps VICIdial responsible for campaign dialing and records while selected answered calls reach the AI agent over SIP. Test it on a dedicated campaign before expanding to other traffic.


**Which VICIdial and Asterisk versions support AI integration?**


Confirm your VICIdial and Asterisk versions, Remote Agent behavior, SIP routing, and header-substitution options against your deployment and SigmaMind AI’s current documentation or support before rollout.[Trillet’s published version range](https://trillet.ai/blogs/vicidial-integration-for-call-centers) describes Trillet’s own validation, not a SigmaMind AI compatibility guarantee.


**What happens if the AI platform goes down?**


Do not assume the documented Remote Agent route automatically falls back to a human queue. Decide how to stop new AI calls, handle calls already in progress, and restore the previous campaign route; implement and test those controls with your VICIdial administrator before production traffic.


**Can the AI agent access lead data during a call?**


SigmaMind AI’s documented route accepts approved VICIdial lead context through X- SIP headers, which become prompt variables. Verify a static header before mapping live lead fields. Writing an AI disposition or summary back to VICIdial requires separately implemented, permissioned middleware and is not an automatic result of sending SIP headers.


**Does multi-tenant isolation protect client data during a pilot?**


VICIdial separates access through user groups and campaign permissions, but its clients can still share the same database and Asterisk infrastructure. Verify whether your SigmaMind AI plan supports separate client workspaces. Restrict VICIdial credentials and reserve capacity for the pilot campaign as well. Those controls reduce cross-client exposure without overstating VICIdial’s native tenant isolation.


## Choosing your path forward


Your technical capacity and need for dialer control should determine the path forward. Keep VICIdial and add SigmaMind AI if you want to retain campaign dialing and can support the documented Remote Agent route. Budget separately for any custom data writeback or warm handoff. Consider an AI-native replacement if VICIdial maintenance consumes too much engineering time or limits campaign changes.


For a SigmaMind AI pilot, register the existing carrier number and map a published agent, then configure the VICIdial user, Remote Agent, carrier prefix, and campaign Routing Extension. Confirm the destination syntax and **Ready** status before controlled calls. Verify SIP-header variables, AMD routing, both systems’ recordings, and native direct transfer; test any custom context handoff, fallback, and rollback separately before expanding traffic.
